feedback.problem: If the path $C$ is a part of the parabola $y=(x+1)^{2}$ traversed from the point $P(0,1)$ to point $Q(1,4),$ then ${\int }_{C}\frac{dx+dy}{y}=$
feedback.worked_solution:
Notice that our curve is given by the explicit Cartesian equation $y=(x+1)^{2}.$ As a result, we obtain the following parametrization of the curve:

$$
\begin{aligned}r(t)=x(t)\,i+y(t)\,j=t\,i+(t+1)^{2}\,j,\,t\in [0,1]\end{aligned}
$$

The derivative of $r(t)$ is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}^{′}(t) & =\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t}\,i+\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}t}\,j=i+2(t+1)\,j.\end{aligned}
$$

We can now evaluate the line integral:

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{C}\frac{dx+dy}{y} & ={\int }_{0}^{1}\frac{1}{y}(\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t}\,\text{d}t+\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}t}\,\text{d}t) \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}\frac{1}{y}(\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t}+\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}t})\text{d}t \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}\frac{1+2(t+1)}{(t+1)^{2}}\,dt \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}\frac{1}{(t+1)^{2}}+\frac{2}{t+1}\,dt \\  & ={[-\frac{1}{t+1}+2\operatorname{ln}⁡(t+1)]}_{0}^{1} \\  & =[-\frac{1}{1+1}+2\operatorname{ln}⁡(1+1)]-[-\frac{1}{0+1}+2\operatorname{ln}⁡(0+1)] \\  & =[-\frac{1}{2}+2\operatorname{ln}⁡2]-[-1+0] \\  & =2\operatorname{ln}⁡2+\frac{1}{2}\end{aligned}
$$
